steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet, and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on a paper towel-lined plate, crumble, and set aside.

Cook and stir onion and celery in the remaining bacon grease over medium heat until the onion is translucent and tender. Drain excess grease, then stir in potatoes. Add water to cover all but 1 inch of the potatoes. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium-low, and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in evaporated milk, and continue cooking until warmed through. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in bacon just before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: This rich and creamy Irish potato soup is loaded with vegetables and smoky bacon for a hearty and flavorsome winter meal.

review.reviewBody: Nice basic potato soup. I used 12 oz. of chicken broth instead of both cans of evapotated milk. At the last, I sauteed half of a huge head of cabbage with the onion, celery and a little garlic in the bacon grease and threw that in once it cooked down a bit. I garnished it with fresh rosemary. Nice simple potato soup with a couple of personal touches.

I have been making potato soup for years and love it. I used to cook the bacon and then add the rest of ingredients all at once and cook for an hour or two. The techniques used in this recipe made such a HUGE difference! I used yellow potatoes and heavy cream instead of evaporated milk, making the smoothest, silkiest broth I’ve ever tasted! The ingredients really pop by sautéing in the bacon grease, and the bacon is so nice and crisp by adding the last 5 minutes with the cream! Thank you! This is my new recipe!

This was good, but needed a bit more flavor. I added a cup of shredded cabbage(cooked with the onion and celery), and a clove of garlic-minced. Also, I used chicken broth instead of water. I agree with some of the other reviews that a whole pound of bacon is too much. Thanks firewife42 for the recipe!

Best tasting potato soup ever! I swapped homemade chicken stock for the water & only used 1/3 # of bacon. The two of us ate it for 3 days & it just kept getting better. Garnishes of thinly sliced green onions & shredded cheddar put it over the top. Thanks so much.

This was a hit at our St. Patrick's Day pot luck today. I reduced the bacon to half a pound, and the evaporated milk to one 13 ounce can. I also substituted homemade chicken broth for the water and peeled my potatoes instead of scrubbing (easier, and I prefer them that way). This all worked out really well. There was not a bit left after the pot luck!
This is a perfectly simple receipe. It taseted better than resturant potato soup for sure. I did add more potatos when I made it, closer to 3 lbs. It still turned out amazing!!

Awesome comfort food! Had to substitute cream of celery soup for celery, heavy cream for evap. milk, I put some dumplings in mine, which helps to thicken the density(goes back to the potato soup my mother made, always put dumplings in hers). Also, shaved carrots are in mine.

Remembered from days of old when my mom fed us(11) on so little money. Chunks of potatoe instead of mashed. Sometimes we had it with no bacon. Maybe she used chicken broth those times but she always made it more Irish with bright green parsley. Thanks for a long saught recipe.
Love potato soup and I am not even Irish. I think the bacon can easlily be cut down to 1/2 pound and also use low-fat evaporated milk to cut the calories.
Exceptional flavor with minimal effort and cost effective!! Definitely a keeper on a cold winter’s day!

WOW...WOW...and WOW... What an amazing recipe, I made it exactly as directed, I was very skeptical, but the flavor blew my taste buds away. No tweaking this recipe for me. Thank you so much for sharing.
It was so good it’s going to be my go to recipe!
I made it ... it's really simple and easy to personalize

It was my first time making a simple soup and I got it perfect. I was nervous and was doubting myself with the flavor. But it turned out great. Simple and easy instructions to follow. So thank you so much for sharing. Need to improve on the thickness of the cream though.
love this recipe (no chicken broth or stock) but has anyone made in a crockpot?? if so could you let me know if any changes to make?
